'''Domantas Sabonis''' ({{IPA|lt|ˈdoːmɐntɐs sɐˈboːnʲɪs}}; born May 3, 1996) is a Lithuanian-American<ref>{{cite news|last=Telander|first=Rick|title=NBA All-Star demographic makes a notable|date=February 18, 2020|newspaper=Chicago Sun-Times|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/2/18/21143414/nba-all-star-game-white-american-players|access-date=April 23, 2020|quote=Sabonis, it should be noted, was born in Portland while his father, Arvydas Sabonis, was playing for the Trail Blazers. But Domantas has dual citizenship and considers Kaunas, Lithuania, home.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Katz|first1=Fred|title=Domantas Sabonis to play in Rising Stars Challenge|url=http://www.normantranscript.com/sports/domantas-sabonis-to-play-in-rising-stars-challenge/article_7280cc1c-e35d-11e6-94f1-0b43d3a02a25.html|work=Norman Transcript|quote=Though he was born in Portland, Ore., Sabonis has dual citizenship and plays for the Lithuanian National Team in international competition}}</ref> professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuanian national team]].<ref name="BioNBA">{{cite web |title=Domantas Sabonis |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1627734/domantas-sabonis/bio |website=NBA.com |access-date=April 15, 2025}}</ref> Son of the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] player [[Arvydas Sabonis]], Sabonis is a two-time [[All-NBA Team]] member, three-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]], and has [[List of NBA annual rebounding leaders|led the league in rebounds]] three times.<ref name="BioNBA" />

Sabonis started his career in Spain with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]]. He then moved to the United States and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. After being drafted 11th overall in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]], Sabonis was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on draft night, spending his rookie season with the team before being traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2017. He played five seasons for the Pacers and was named an All-Star twice during his tenure. In 2022, Sabonis was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for [[Tyrese Haliburton]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McKenney |first1=Jack |title=Domantas Sabonis, Tyrese Haliburton trade has been a win-win|url=https://fansided.com/2022/12/02/tyrese-haliburton-domantas-sabonis-win-win/ |website=Fansided |date=December 2, 2022 |access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> Named to his first All-NBA team and third All-Star selection in 2023, he led the Kings alongside [[De'Aaron Fox]] to the third seed in the [[2023 NBA playoffs]] and helped them break their [[List of NBA franchise post-season droughts#Longest post-season droughts in team history|NBA record 16-season playoff drought]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Razo |first1=Eduardo |title=Fox ready to help Kings get over hump, break playoff 'curse' |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/deaaron-fox-ready-help-kings-get-over-hump-break-nba-playoff-curse |website=NBC Sports |date=October 18, 2022 |access-date=February 5, 2023}}</ref>

==Early life==
Domantas was born on May 3, 1996, in [[Portland, Oregon]], when his father, [[Arvydas Sabonis]], was playing for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Misevičius |first1=Laurynas R. |title=Patriotiškumo pavyzdys: kaip JAV gimęs D. Sabonis savo gimtuoju miestu pavertė Kauną |url=https://www.delfi.lt/krepsinis/herojai/patriotiskumo-pavyzdys-kaip-jav-gimes-d-sabonis-savo-gimtuoju-miestu-paverte-kauna.d?id=70411676 |website=[[DELFI]] |access-date=February 16, 2020 |language=lt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Holmes |first1=Baxter |title=NBA All-Star Domantas Sabonis, his legendary father Arvydas -- and the enormous weight of legacy |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/story/_/id/42911487/nba-all-star-domantas-sabonis-legendary-father-arvydas-enormous-weight-legacy |website=[[ESPN]] |date=December 12, 2024 |access-date=17 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Domantas Sabonis - Men's Basketball |url=https://gozags.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/domantas-sabonis/366 |website=Gonzaga University Athletics |access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref><ref name="BioNBA"/> His mother is [[:lt:Ingrida Mikelionytė|Ingrida Mikelionytė]], the first Miss Lithuania in 1988.<ref>{{cite web|title=All in the Sabonis family |url= https://www.nba.com/news/domantas-sabonis-all-star |website=NBA.com |date=February 14, 2020}}</ref> He has two older brothers, Žygimantas (born 1991) and [[Tautvydas Sabonis|Tautvydas]] (born 1992), and a younger sister, Aušrinė (born 1997).<ref name="urb">{{cite web |last1=Urbonas |first1=Donatas |title=Nepriklausomybės vaiko pavyzdys: D.Sabonio fenomenas prasidėjo Sabonių namuose |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/nba/nepriklausomybes-vaiko-pavyzdys-d-sabonio-fenomenas-prasidejo-saboniu-namuose-1130-1275680 |website=[[15min.lt]] |access-date=February 16, 2020 |language=lt |date=November 11, 2019}}</ref> When Arvydas was once asked if any of his sons will follow his footsteps in basketball, he singled out Domantas due to his stubbornness, and because he is [[left-handed]].<ref name="urb"/>

In 2004, Domantas' father retired from basketball, and whole family moved from Portland to [[Málaga]], Spain.

==Professional career==

===Unicaja (2012–2014)===
Despite being only a 16-year-old, on September 5, 2012, Sabonis debuted for [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] against [[Cibona Zagreb]].<ref>[https://www.basketnews.lt/news-53417-sabonis-debiutavo-unicaja-komandoje.html Sabonis debiutavo 'Unicaja' komandoje]</ref> He was later loaned to [[CB Axarquía|Clínicas Rincón]] for the 2012–13 season. He returned to Málaga for the 2013–14 season and debuted in the [[Liga ACB]] on October 13, 2013,<ref>[http://www.krepsinis.net/naujiena/unicaja-su-d-saboniu-ir-m-kuzminsku-pergale-pradejo-ispanijos-cempionata/234275 'Unicaja' su D.Saboniu ir M.Kuzminsku pergale pradėjo Ispanijos čempionatą]</ref> becoming the youngest Unicaja player to debut in the ACB (17 years, 5 months and 10 days).<ref>[http://www.krepsinis.net/naujiena/d-sabonis-tapo-jauniausiu-ispanijos-cempionate-zaidusiu-unicaja-zaideju/234290 D.Sabonis tapo jauniausiu Ispanijos čempionate žaidusiu 'Unicaja' žaidėju]</ref> On October 18, Sabonis debuted in the [[EuroLeague]] against [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]]. In February 2014, he finished in the top 10 for the 2013 [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award]] voting.<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_,qIYgqUhJ-Ue6pPZvVE7q1.articleMode_on.html SARIC IS 2013 YOUNG MEN'S POY]</ref> His best ACB game came on May 3, when he scored 13 points on 100% shooting.<ref>[https://www.basketnews.lt/news-73138-per-18aji-gimtadieni-sabonis-suzaide-geriausias-sezono-rungtynes.html Per 18–ąjį gimtadienį Sabonis sužaidė geriausias sezono rungtynes]</ref> On May 10, Sabonis helped Unicaja's junior team win the Spain Youth Basketball League silver medal. In the final game, he recorded 14 points and eight rebounds.<ref>[https://www.basketnews.lt/news-73315-sabonis-su-unicaja-ispanijos-jaunimo-pirmenybese-iskovojo-sidabro-medalius.html Sabonis su 'Unicaja' Ispanijos jaunimo pirmenybėse iškovojo sidabro medalius]</ref> In January 2015, he finished in the top 5 for the 2014 FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award voting.<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_VUv2HC68IKQHKl,DKDnXz1.articleMode_on.html SARIC IS 2014 YOUNG MEN'S POY]</ref> During his time with Unicaja, he never signed a professional contract with salary in order to remain eligible for the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]].<ref>[http://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/archyvas/domantas-sabonis-prisijungs-prie-pagrindines-unicaja-komandos-872-359169 Domantas Sabonis prisijungs prie pagrindinės 'Unicaja' komandos]</ref>

====2023–24 season====
On December 18, Sabonis logged the 35th triple-double of his career with 28 points, 13 rebounds and 12 assists in a 143–131 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Another triple-double for Domantas Sabonis sends Kings past Wizards 143-131|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584986|website=ESPN.com|date=December 18, 2023|access-date=December 19, 2023}}</ref> On January 3, 2024, Sabonis recorded a triple-double with 22 points, a then season-high 23 rebounds and 12 assists in a 138–135 double overtime win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 3, 2024 |title=Kings outlast short-handed Magic in double overtime behind triple-double from Domantas Sabonis |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585104 |access-date=January 4, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On January 29, Sabonis scored 20 points on 10-of-11 shooting from the field, grabbed a career-high 26 rebounds and delivered five assists in a 103–94 win against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He became the second player in NBA history with at least 20 points, 25 rebounds, five assists and a shooting percentage of 90% or better. The other was [[Wilt Chamberlain]], who did it six times.<ref>{{cite web |title=Domantas Sabonis has career-high 26 rebounds as Kings shut out Grizzlies late for 103-94 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585291 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=February 15, 2024}}</ref>

On February 13, Sabonis posted his 50th career triple-double with 35 points, 18 rebounds, 12 assists and three blocks in a 130–125 loss against the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 13, 2024 |title=Kevin Durant scores 28, Devin Booker adds 25, Suns outlast Kings 130-125 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585402 |access-date=February 15, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On March 12, Sabonis recorded his 47th consecutive double-double with 22 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists in a 129–94 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He surpassed [[Jerry Lucas]]' previous record of 46 to become the [[Sacramento Kings]] franchise leader in consecutive double-doubles in a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-domantas-sabonis-breaks-55-year-old-record-with-stunning-performance-vs-bucks|title=Kings' Domantas Sabonis breaks 55-year-old record with stunning performance vs Bucks|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=March 13, 2024|access-date=March 20, 2024}}</ref> On March 25, Sabonis had 11 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists to become the fifth player in NBA history with at least 25 triple-doubles in a season, joining [[Nikola Jokić]], [[Russell Westbrook]], Wilt Chamberlain and [[Oscar Robertson]]. He also posted his 54th consecutive double-double, breaking a tie with [[Kevin Love]] for the longest streak since the 1976–77 merger between the NBA and ABA.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 25, 2024 |title=Sabonis' milestone night helps the Kings beat the 76ers 108-96 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585670 |access-date=March 26, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=March 25, 2024 |title=Domantas Sabonis sets post-merger double-double streak amid Kings' playoff push |url=https://www.nba.com/news/domantas-sabonis-double-double-streak |access-date=March 26, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 9, this streak would end as Sabonis had eight points and 13 rebounds in a 112-105 loss against the Oklahoma City Thunder, peaking at 61 consecutive double-doubles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 10, 2024 |title=Sabonis' double-double streak ends at 61 in Kings' loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39911469/sabonis-double-double-streak-ends-61-kings-loss |access-date=May 19, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2024–25 season====
On June 14, 2024, the Sacramento Kings announced that Sabonis would switch to No. 11 jersey to honor his father, [[Arvydas Sabonis]], who wore the same number during his time with the Portland Trail Blazers. The Sacramento Kings had previously retired No. 11 to honor [[Bob Davies]]. However, Davies' children gave their blessing for Sabonis to use the [[retired number]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 14, 2024 |title=Domantas Sabonis to Wear No. 11 for the Sacramento Kings |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/domantas-sabonis-to-wear-no-11-for-the-sacramento-kings |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 26, Sabonis posted his 59th career triple-double with 29 points, 12 rebounds, 10 assists in 131–127 loss against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He tied [[Larry Bird]] for the 10th-most triple-doubles in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web|title=LeBron James records triple-double, Davis scores 31 in Lakers' 131-127 win over Kings|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704662|website=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 31, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Domantas Sabonis ties Larry Bird for the 10th-most triple-doubles in NBA history|url=https://hoopshype.com/2024/10/27/domantas-sabonis-ties-larry-bird-for-the-10th-most-triple-doubles-in-nba-history/|website=HoopsHype.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 31, 2024}}</ref> On November 6, Sabonis posted a triple-double with 17 points, 13 assists, and 11 rebounds in a 122–107 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He became the first player in NBA history to post a triple-double without a missed field goal, a turnover, and a foul.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-domantas-sabonis-makes-nba-history-with-stat-line-vs-raptors|title=Domantas Sabonis makes NBA history with remarkable stat line vs. Raptors|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=November 6, 2024|access-date=November 8, 2024}}</ref> On December 12, Sabonis recorded a season-high 32 points and 20 rebounds on 11-of-15 shooting from the field and 9-of-9 from the free throw line in a 111–109 victory over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web |date=December 12, 2024 |title=Sabonis has season-high 32 points and 20 rebounds to lead Kings to a 111-109 win over Pelicans |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401736801 |access-date=December 12, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On January 7, 2025, Sabonis was selected as the Lithuanian Basketball Player of the Year for a fifth time.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cubera |first1=Paulius |title=Geriausi 2024 metų Lietuvos krepšininkai – Domantas Sabonis ir Gerda Raulušaitytė |url=https://ltu.basketball/geriausi-2024-metu-lietuvos-krepsininkai-domantas-sabonis-ir-gerda-raulusaityte/ |website=Lietuvos krepšinis |access-date=August 17, 2025 |language=lt-LT |date=January 7, 2025}}</ref> On January 10, Sabonis logged 23 points and a career-high 28 rebounds in a 114–97 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Domantas Sabonis has 23 points and career-high 28 rebounds as Kings rally to beat Celtics 114-97 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401705094 |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=January 11, 2025}}</ref> On February 13, Sabonis tied his career-high with 28 rebounds, along with 22 points and five assists in a 140–133 overtime loss against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=McCollum scores 43 points to lift Pelicans over the Kings 140-133 in overtime |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705351 |access-date=February 14, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=February 13, 2025}}</ref> On April 11, Sabonis had 19 points, 16 rebounds and five assists in 101–100 loss against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He became the sixth player since the ABA/NBA merger to have 60 or more double-doubles for three consecutive seasons, joining [[Moses Malone]], [[John Stockton]], [[Tim Duncan]], [[Kevin Garnett]] and [[Dwight Howard]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clippers hold off Kings 101-100 to remain tied with Nuggets for No. 4 in tight Western Conference |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705750 |access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |date=April 12, 2025}}</ref>

====2025–26 season====
After missing the season opener on October 22, 2025, against the Phoenix Suns due to injury, Sabonis returned to the Kings' lineup in the next game on October 24. He scored 12 points, grabbed a game-high 12 rebounds, and made a put-back with 6.4 seconds remaining, securing a 105–104 victory over the Utah Jazz.<ref>{{cite web |title=Domantas Sabonis' late put-back gives Kings 1-point win over Jazz |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/domantas-sabonis-late-put-back-gives-kings-1-point-win-over-jazz--flm-2025-10-25/ |website=Reuters |date=October 25, 2025}}</ref> On November 14, Sabonis scored a season-high 34 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in a 124–110 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Timberwolves 124, Kings 110 – Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401809786 |website=ESPN |date=November 14, 2025 |access-date=November 14, 2025}}</ref> However, on November 19, Sabonis missed a game against the Oklahoma City Thunder due to a partially [[meniscus tear|torn meniscus]] and was subsequently ruled out for at least three-to-four weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Big blow for Kings: Sabonis torn meniscus, will be re-evaluated in 3-4 weeks |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1897143/big-blow-for-kings-sabonis-torn-meniscus-will-be-re-evaluated-in-3-4-weeks/ |website=Eurohoops.net |access-date=November 30, 2025 |date=November 20, 2025}}</ref> On December 19, it was announced that he would miss four-to-five more weeks in recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kings' Domantas Sabonis out another month with knee injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47362453/kings-domantas-sabonis-another-month-knee-injury |access-date=January 3, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |date=December 19, 2025}}</ref> On January 16, 2026, Sabonis returned to the Kings' lineup after two months of recovery from an injury and by contributing 13 points, six rebounds, five assists helped his team to achieve a 128–115 victory over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Po dviejų mėnesių traumos D. Sabonis sugrįžo: "Kings" susitvarkė su Rytų konferencijos autsaideriais |url=https://www.lrytas.lt/sportas/krepsinis/2026/01/17/news/po-dvieju-menesiu-traumos-d-sabonis-sugrizo-kings-susitvarke-su-rytu-konferencijos-autsaideriais-40989819 |website=[[Lrytas.lt]] |access-date=January 31, 2026 |language=lt-LT |date=January 17, 2026}}</ref> On February 18, Sabonis underwent a season-ending surgery to repair his [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kalland |first1=Robby |title=Kings stars Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine have season-ending surgeries amid disastrous year in Sacramento |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/kings-domantas-sabonis-zach-lavine-injuries-season-ending-surgeries/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=April 5, 2026 |date=February 18, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sabonis married Shashana Rosen on August 15, 2021, in [[Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat]], France; the wedding was officiated by a rabbi.<ref name="Jewish">{{Cite news |last=Esensten|first=Andrew|date=April 12, 2023 |title=Sacramento Kings' Domantas Sabonis is joining Team Jewish |url=https://jweekly.com/2023/04/12/kings-domantas-sabonis-is-also-on-team-jewish/ |newspaper=J}}</ref> They have three children: a son named Tiger, born on March 11, 2022, a daughter named Eleven Rose, born July 11, 2023, and a son named Tauras Levi, born in June, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sacks |first=Hannah |date=June 5, 2025 |title=NBA's Domantas Sabonis Welcomes Baby No. 3 with Wife Shashana: 'Soaking in Every Little Moment' |url=https://people.com/nba-domantas-sabonis-welcomes-baby-no-3-with-wife-shashana-exclusive-11748763 |website=People}}</ref> The family keeps [[Shabbat]] and eats only [[kosher food]].<ref name="Jewish" /> In April 2023, his wife announced that Sabonis was in the process of converting to [[Judaism]].<ref name="Jewish" /> Sabonis and his wife launched a wine brand in November 2024, dubbed ''Ones by Sabonis''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.winebusiness.com/news/link/295099|title=Three-time NBA All-star Domantas Sabonis & Entrepreneur Shashana Sabonis Launch Ones By Sabonis|work=Wine Business|date=November 15, 2024|accessdate=November 18, 2024}}</ref>
